# REPLY TO LEGAL NOTICE

To,
[ADVOCATE NAME]
[COUNSEL FOR SUPPLIER]

Subject: Reply to legal notice dated [DATE OF NOTICE] on behalf of [YOUR NAME / SHOP NAME], Jaipur regarding alleged dues of Rs. 1,20,000.

Sir/Madam,

1. I am in receipt of your legal notice dated [DATE OF NOTICE] sent on behalf of your client [SUPPLIER NAME], demanding a sum of Rs. 1,20,000 towards alleged dues for goods.

2. The contents of your notice are false, baseless, and denied in entirety, except as specifically admitted herein.

3. At the outset, it is stated that I have already made a part payment of Rs. 70,000 towards the order via NEFT on [DATE OF NEFT PAYMENT]. This part payment is duly reflected in bank records [[ICA1872:s50]].

4. Furthermore, as per the contract between the parties [[ICA1872:s37]], your client was bound to deliver the full consignment of goods. However, the remaining goods were never delivered to my shop. Under the law, payment cannot be claimed when reciprocal promises of delivery are unfulfilled [[ICA1872:s51]].

5. In view of the above facts, no amount of Rs. 1,20,000 is due or payable by me. The demand made in your notice is completely untenable.

6. I call upon your client to withdraw the said legal notice immediately.

Yours faithfully,

[YOUR NAME]
[SHOP NAME]
Jaipur, Rajasthan

claims.claim: A part payment made via NEFT is a valid method of fulfilling a contractual promise and is recognized by law.
claims.reason: Section 50 states that the performance of a promise may be made in any manner prescribed or sanctioned by the promisee, and Illustration (a) specifically confirms that a bank transfer is a valid form of payment.
claims.exact_quote: This part payment is duly reflected in bank records [[ICA1872:s50]].

claims.claim: Parties to a contract are legally obligated to perform the promises they have made.
claims.reason: Section 37 mandates that the parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises.
claims.exact_quote: Furthermore, as per the contract between the parties [[ICA1872:s37]], your client was bound to deliver the full consignment of goods.

claims.claim: In a contract with reciprocal promises, a party is not required to perform their part if the other party fails to fulfill their reciprocal promise.
claims.reason: Section 51 provides that when a contract consists of reciprocal promises to be simultaneously performed, no promisor need perform his promise unless the promisee is ready and willing to perform his reciprocal promise.
claims.exact_quote: Under the law, payment cannot be claimed when reciprocal promises of delivery are unfulfilled [[ICA1872:s51]].

claims.claim: Payment via NEFT counts as performance of a contract when done in a manner prescribed or sanctioned by the other party.
claims.reason: Section 50 states that performance may be made in any manner sanctioned by the promisee, and illustration (a) specifically clarifies that a bank transfer constitutes valid payment.
claims.exact_quote: You have already paid Rs 70,000 via NEFT, which can be proved through your bank statement / transaction receipt [[ICA1872:s50]].

claims.claim: A person is not required to pay for goods if the seller fails to deliver them as part of their reciprocal promise.
claims.reason: Section 51 states that a promisor is not bound to perform unless the promisee is ready and willing to perform their reciprocal promise, such as delivering goods in exchange for payment.
claims.exact_quote: Furthermore, under contract law, a supplier cannot demand full payment when they failed to deliver the rest of the goods [[ICA1872:s51]].
